instruction: Fill the empty Student name cells C8 through C11 with the name from C7 in the open spreadsheet.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to fill blank cells in B1:E30 by selecting column ranges and using fill-down (Ctrl+D). Successfully filled column B Level values in some ranges but incorrectly applied fill-down to column C, overwriting student names. Eventually closed the file without completing the task correctly.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Calc, select cell ranges using Name Box, type values, use Ctrl+D fill-down, interact with menus
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed because it used blanket fill-down on entire columns instead of selective filling. It filled C2:C30 with 'Blake Dreary' instead of filling each student's name only within their row group. The -0.2 score indicates data corruption.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed to filling Student name in 4 cells within one student group. Tests the model's ability to fill a small range in column C without corrupting other student names. C7 contains 'Arnold Shawarma' and C8:C11 are blank.
metadata.explanation: Task requires filling C8:C11 with 'Arnold Shawarma' (the value from C7). Getter reads values of C8-C11, metric awards 0.25 partial credit per correct cell.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads cells C8, C9, C10, C11 from the xlsx file using openpyxl, matching the instruction's target cells.
Metric correctly handles the expected parameter as the rules dict directly (expected.get('expected_value')), consistent with type='rule' framework behavior.
Expected value 'Arnold Shawarma' matches the metadata stating C7 contains this name, which the instruction requires to be copied to C8:C11.
Partial credit scoring (0.25 per cell) is appropriate for a 4-cell fill task, allowing meaningful partial evaluation.
Postconfig correctly activates the window and saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.
Complete coverage: all 4 cells specified in the instruction are verified with correct expected values.
